title: 【PUA解密系列】美国小伙黑化成为PUA祖师爷

coverage.dedup: new against 202 formal sources; highest 12-character shingle containment 0.219%

timeline.summary: A provocative opening uses clips about a Chinese coaching company and the 2019 anti-PUA controversy, then defines PUA as 'pick-up artist' and promises an origin story.
timeline.speaker: Mikey narration plus unidentified inserted clips

timeline.summary: English street/interview excerpts lead into a narrated account of late-1980s Los Angeles and Ross Jeffries as an awkward outsider who became an early PUA figure.
timeline.speaker: embedded English speakers followed by Mikey narration

timeline.summary: The video characterizes NLP as therapeutic 'brain code' for trauma and says Jeffries reverse-engineered it to implant attraction; this medical and causal account is presented without sources.
timeline.speaker: Mikey narration

timeline.summary: Mikey disputes a simple villain-origin story, framing early participants as socially excluded men seeking relief from fear and rejection, then asks whether a psychological tool leads to happiness or deeper harm.
timeline.speaker: Mikey narration and interpretation

timeline.summary: He attributes 'speed seduction' to Jeffries and describes anchoring and embedded commands: eliciting emotion, pairing it with a gesture or voice, and later re-triggering it. He asserts online users tested the method and found it effective.
timeline.speaker: Mikey narration; historical and efficacy claims unverified

timeline.summary: The video interprets the technique as bypassing ordinary value exchange and producing a sense of control for insecure men; broad claims about unconscious defenses and emotional hijacking are offered as mechanism.
timeline.speaker: Mikey narration

timeline.summary: Mikey attributes a regretful birthday statement to Jeffries about losing the ability to love, then connects internet growth, sexual liberation and male dating anxiety to later industry expansion.
timeline.speaker: Mikey narration and an alleged third-party quotation

timeline.summary: He calls PUA and tools neutral but asks whether the user controls the tool or vice versa, says hypnosis was too difficult for ordinary people, and previews a later formula based on negs and performance.
timeline.speaker: Mikey narration

claims.speaker: Mikey as narrator
claims.statement: He says a 2019 online anti-PUA campaign was followed by coordinated bans of Langji Qinggan accounts and the collapse of a major Chinese PUA business.
claims.conditions: A dated platform, audience and business-history claim requiring contemporaneous platform notices and corporate records.

claims.speaker: Mikey as narrator
claims.statement: He distinguishes the loanword PUA/'pick-up artist' from the later public shorthand of pressure and coercive control.
claims.conditions: A terminology/history distinction; it does not neutralize manipulative practices described later.

claims.speaker: Mikey as narrator
claims.statement: He claims NLP originated as a scientifically grounded treatment used by psychologists for veterans' PTSD and can overwrite painful memories through language and body cues.
claims.conditions: High-impact medical and scientific claim that is materially oversimplified and unsupported in the package; do not treat as clinical fact or advice.

claims.speaker: Mikey as narrator
claims.statement: He credits Ross Jeffries with turning NLP ideas into 'speed seduction' around 1988 by moving therapeutic or hypnotic techniques into bars and street interactions.
claims.conditions: Priority, date, authorship and the link to clinical practice require primary historical sources.

claims.speaker: Mikey as narrator
claims.statement: He describes anchoring and embedded commands as pairing a person's emotional high with a gesture or voice so that the emotion can later be triggered and misattributed as attraction.
claims.conditions: Manipulation-oriented mechanism and efficacy claim; the video provides no controlled evidence, and it must not become an instruction for covert influence.

claims.speaker: Mikey as narrator
claims.statement: He says early forum users rapidly tested the techniques and found them effective.
claims.conditions: Anecdotal field reports are subject to selection, reporting and outcome bias and do not establish effectiveness or consent.

claims.speaker: Mikey as narrator
claims.statement: He interprets technique-centered dating as an attempt to bypass ordinary value exchange and gain an addictive sense of control over other people's emotions.
claims.conditions: This is Mikey's moral/psychological interpretation, not a diagnosis of all practitioners or proof of an 'emotional hijack' mechanism.

claims.speaker: Mikey as narrator quoting Ross Jeffries
claims.statement: He attributes to Jeffries a statement that using techniques with many women left him unable to love and in great pain.
claims.conditions: Sensitive third-party quotation and mental-state claim; exact wording, occasion and source are not shown and require the original recording or transcript.

claims.speaker: Mikey as narrator
claims.statement: He links internet expansion, sexual-liberation/feminist movements and male dating anxiety to a PUA industry allegedly worth hundreds of millions of dollars.
claims.conditions: Broad social causation and financial-scale claim without citations or accounts; keep only as attributed narration.

claims.speaker: Mikey
claims.statement: He concludes that a tool can come to control its user, and treats the history as a warning about dependence on manipulation techniques.
claims.conditions: Usable only as a high-level interpretation separated from the video's unsupported historical, medical and efficacy claims.

examples.summary: The video illustrates alleged anchoring with a repeated glass tap or low voice at an emotional peak; this is a narrated technique claim, not demonstrated evidence.
examples.limits: Do not convert into covert-influence instructions.

examples.summary: An alleged late-life regret quotation is used as the cautionary outcome of technique obsession.
examples.limits: Original quote and context are missing.

speaker_attribution.speaker: Mikey
speaker_attribution.basis: Primary Chinese documentary narrator and closing self-identification; he is interpreting third-party history rather than recounting his own direct observation.

speaker_attribution.speaker: opening Chinese clip speaker
speaker_attribution.basis: Frame 000001 and S00001-S00010 show an unidentified man making promotional claims; this is inserted material, not Mikey's statement.

speaker_attribution.speaker: embedded English speakers
speaker_attribution.basis: S00049-S00058 and sampled archival/street footage contain English voices; identity and original context were not established.

speaker_attribution.speaker: Ross Jeffries and other historical figures
speaker_attribution.basis: Mostly represented through Mikey's narration, public/archival images, books and alleged quotations; no complete primary interview is supplied.

visual_findings: All 12 sampled frames were opened and reviewed. Frame 000001 is a third-party Chinese talking-head clip, while frames 000002-000012 are a documentary montage of street footage, UCLA/Rose Bowl imagery, dramatized footage, a presenter in Paris, computers, a report screen, a book and an archival clip.
Frame 000007 shows a kiss with faces partially blocked as illustrative footage; it does not establish consent, outcome or the historical technique being narrated.
Frames 000008-000009 show report/database-like screens, but the sparse images are not legible or sourced enough to verify dates, field reports, identities or efficacy.
Frame 000012 labels Neil Strauss and Tynan/Herbal T in an archival clip. Sparse sampling cannot establish who speaks at each moment or whether subtitles accurately preserve the source context.

permissions.speaker_restriction: Mikey may be identified only as the narrator of attributed interpretations. Inserted speakers, alleged quotations and third-party biography remain separate.
permissions.safety_restriction: No anchoring, embedded-command, hypnosis, emotional-trigger or covert-control description may be converted into actionable interpersonal advice.
permissions.reuse_policy: New research-source candidate; no formal weight until historical, scientific and attribution review passes.

limitations: The complete automatic transcript was read but not checked word-for-word against original audio; many names and technical terms are ASR-corrupted.
Twelve 45-second sparse frames are not continuous audio-visual review and cannot align every quotation, speaker or archival image.
The package contains no bibliography or primary sources for the historical, medical, financial and efficacy claims.
Dramatized, stock, public and archival clips illustrate the narration but do not independently corroborate it.
